comments.author: @TheEarthEngineOfficial
comments.text: The Yamal detail is the one that stuck with me — a frozen tundra of half a million people ending up richer per person than Norway in the flipped world. It makes the video's real point land harder: unity buys power, but the competition between neighbours is what made Europe rich in the first place.

replies.author: @TheEarthEngineOfficial
replies.text: @IvanLapshin_tmnThat's the fun stress-test of the video's own logic — if competition between neighbours is what made Europe rich, more neighbours should mean more wealth. But the other half of the argument is the catch: 500 states would also mean 500 borders, 500 currencies and 500 armies to pay for. Where do you think the balance tips — is there a number of states where the competition stops paying for the friction?
